name: Cairn-Ecliptic
specific_features: Monolithic structures of unknown origin: three hundred stone cairns stacked in a line that matches this system's ecliptic plane to within a fraction of a degree
Buried megastructure: thermal imaging shows a heat source four kilometers wide beneath the southern ice sheet, stable for as long as instruments have watched
Automated beacon transmitting a repeating sequence of prime numbers from beneath the megastructure
description: A bone-white moon-world locked in deep freeze, its surface a quilt of fractured ice sheets and methane lakes frozen mid-ripple. A single vast impact crater dominates the northern hemisphere, its rim cast in permanent shadow, and meteor scars run in braided channels toward the south pole. Nothing moves, and nothing has moved here for geological ages.

Standing on the ice is standing inside silence. There is no air to carry sound, only the creak of your own suit and the faint tick of frost forming on your visor. Starlight comes hard and unfiltered, and the cairns throw shadows so sharp they look cut into the ice rather than laid across it.

Three hundred cairns march across the southern hemisphere in a perfectly straight line, each stack of dark stone identical to the last, each older than the crater that should have destroyed them. They align with the ecliptic—the plane of every orbiting body in the system—to a tolerance no natural process explains. Beneath them, four kilometers down, something warm is waiting, and it counts primes at anyone who listens.

No wreck, no settlement, no fossil marks this world; the builders left nothing but the stones and the heat below. Core-mining consortiums want the exotic matter readings confirmed before they commit, but every probe sent toward the heat source fails at the same depth, logging the same impossible reading first. Surveyors have started refusing night shifts, noting privately that the beacon's sequence changed by one number last month—and no one can prove it wasn't counting down.
